title: Notification Delivery Truth
lede: The Notifications screen now tells the truth when account delivery is paused or this device is not registered, while keeping the durable in-app inbox available and giving the person a recoverable path.

stats.n: Measured from the matched top captures: Delivery card top moves 1308px → 1963px at the device's 3.07px/pt scale
Resume now is visible while the account is paused
Preference, pause, iOS permission, APNs registration, and current token

sections.heading: Matched screenshots
sections.note: Both columns use the same local paused-account fixture, iPhone 16 Pro simulator, UI-test steps, and scroll positions. The baseline uses the pre-change screen from HEAD; the after capture uses the restored final source.

pairs.title: Top of Notifications
pairs.sub: The delivery summary and account pause are the first decision points.
pairs.beforeCap: The paused fixture still reads “Push alerts are enabled,” and no account pause or Resume action is visible.
pairs.afterCap: The same account reads “Paused until …,” keeps the inbox promise visible, and offers Resume now alongside the APNs recovery state.

pairs.title: Delivery and notification types
pairs.sub: The self-test must not bypass the same delivery policy the screen reports.
pairs.beforeCap: The Push alerts switch stands alone; a paused account has no explanation for why a device self-test is unavailable.
pairs.afterCap: The switch is qualified while paused, the test is withheld with a reason, and category choices explain that they apply after resume.

changesNote: This slice closes the two native notification findings that shared an existing server contract; it does not claim APNs delivery or physical-device acceptance.

changes.h: Account pause is now visible and reversible
changes.was: A future pausedUntil value was silently ignored, so the native screen could promise enabled delivery while the server suppressed push and email.
changes.now: Quiet hours shows the active end time, exposes Pause 1 hour/day/week when clear, and gives a one-tap Resume now action. The in-app inbox remains explicitly available.

changes.h: The device self-test follows ordinary delivery eligibility
changes.was: The test button appeared whenever iOS allowed push and a token string existed, even when the account was paused, Push alerts were off, or APNs registration had failed.
changes.now: The test requires Push alerts on, no active pause, iOS authorization, a server-accepted registration, and the current installation token; otherwise the screen names the next recovery action.

changes.h: Preference failures are no longer silent
changes.was: A failed toggle save reverted the optimistic switch and stored an error, but the loaded settings screen never rendered or announced that error.
changes.now: Loaded save errors render inline with Reload, announce through VoiceOver, and clear before the next save attempt while preserving the safe revert.

verification: 17 focused source-contract tests pass across the five affected iOS notification/settings suites.
Native build: Wisconsin Debug builds successfully for iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 26.5, with code signing disabled.
Matched UI capture: NotificationSettingsScreenshotUITests passes for both the HEAD baseline and final after source; each run exports the same two named screenshots.
Artifact inspection: all four exported PNGs were read before inclusion; the measured Delivery-card displacement is reported above rather than inferred from visual scale.
Environment note: the first sandboxed build stopped before compilation on a Swift Package Manager cache permission error; the same build succeeded with host Xcode/cache access.
notes: This is deterministic fixture proof, not authenticated production proof. Real APNs delivery, notification permission changes, and physical-device acceptance remain separate gates.
The baseline and after captures were run at different wall-clock minutes, so the simulator clock differs; preference data, device, fixture, and UI actions were held constant.
Account deletion remains parked until the product accepts the historical-custody and erasure/pseudonymization contract documented in the remediation plan.
